text: Starting on mobile pinch-zoom crash. Bringing up preview server on 4223 and building a touch probe.

Pixel 5 CDP touch probe runs clean for page errors and NaN camera, but found a hard freeze: if two fingers land at the same point, initialPinchDistance is 0, the touchmove guard tests it for truthiness, and pinch is dead for the whole gesture. Now measuring heap and layer pressure for the actual crash.

60 sustained fast pinch cycles on a 40 node board: zero page errors, heap flat at 3.7MB, no renderer crash, DOM node count constant. So this is not a JS leak. Moving to a randomized multi finger fuzzer to find the state where the board stops responding.

80 iterations of randomized 1 to 3 finger fuzzing, every one followed by a pinch and pan health check: all 80 passed on Chromium. The board state machine does not wedge. Installing WebKit to test the iPhone engine, since mobile Safari has different touch semantics.

Found it. A two finger pinch where the second finger lands on a markdown note body never starts: the note body calls stopPropagation on touchstart, so the viewport listener that begins the pinch never runs. Measured on a Pixel 5 emulation: scale stays at 1.01999 and zero of 16 touchmoves are defaultPrevented, versus all 16 prevented and a clean zoom to 2.0 when a finger lands on the background. No preventDefault is why it looks like a crash on a real phone, the browser takes the gesture and zooms the whole page.

Fix proven in the running page. With the multi touch case allowed past stopPropagation, a pinch with both fingers on a markdown note goes from scale 1.0 to 1.63 with 20 of 20 touchmoves prevented, versus 1.0 to 1.0 with 0 of 20 prevented before. Second defect also proven: the touchmove guard tests initialPinchDistance for truthiness, so a 0px baseline kills the gesture and the repair branch below it is unreachable. 0px apart is dead, 1px apart zooms to 5. Ordinary background pinch and one finger pan unchanged.

Done. Root cause is four node bodies calling stopPropagation on every touchstart, which hides multi touch starts from the viewport listener that begins a pinch. The gesture then gets no preventDefault at all, so the browser takes it, which is the mobile crash. Patch is five one line edits in braindump.js, no CSS. Port 4223 released, nothing written outside my scratch dir and this feed.
